figures.shows: Original Inception module (left) and SE-Inception module (right): the module output (HxWxC) goes through global pooling (1x1xC), FC (1x1xC/r), ReLU, FC (1x1xC), Sigmoid, then Scale of the module output.

figures.shows: Four panels of top-1 error (%) against epoch (0 to 100) for train and val curves of baselines and SE counterparts (ResNet-50, ResNet-152, ResNeXt-50, BN-Inception). figures.shows: Five integration designs: (a) residual block, (b) standard SE block (SE after Residual, before summation), (c) SE-PRE (SE before Residual), (d) SE-POST (SE after the summation), (e) SE-Identity (SE on the identity connection parallel to Residual).

papers.what_it_is: The paper proposes the Squeeze-and-Excitation block for channel-wise feature recalibration in CNNs and evaluates it on ImageNet, CIFAR, Places365, COCO and ILSVRC 2017, with ablations and an analysis of the excitation activations.

assertions.value: The authors define the SE block as a computational unit built on a transformation that maps an input to feature maps. A squeeze step produces a channel descriptor by global average pooling over the spatial dimensions. An excitation step turns it into per-channel weights that rescale the feature maps.
quotes: A Squeeze-and-Excitation block is a computational unit
This is achieved by using global average pooling to generate channel-wise statistics.
rescaling U with the activations s
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the block and its squeeze, excitation and scale operations in Section 3.

assertions.value: The authors state that the excitation is a sigmoid gating mechanism, a bottleneck of two fully-connected layers around a ReLU, with reduction ratio r, to limit model complexity and aid generalisation.
quotes: s = Fex(z, W) = σ(g(z, W)) = σ(W2δ(W1z))
a bottleneck with two fully-connected (FC) layers around
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper gives the excitation equation and its parameterisation.

assertions.value: The authors state that the excitation function must learn a non-mutually-exclusive relationship, so that multiple channels can be emphasised rather than a one-hot activation, which motivates the sigmoid gate.
quotes: it must learn a non-mutually-exclusive relationship since we would like to ensure that multiple channels are allowed to be emphasised
assertions.certainty_reason: Design criterion stated by the authors in Section 3.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that in SE-ResNet the SE block transformation is the non-identity branch of a residual module, and that squeeze and excitation both act before summation with the identity branch.
quotes: is taken to be the non-identity branch of a residual module
Squeeze and Excitation both act before summation with the identity branch.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own SE-ResNet construction.

assertions.value: The authors claim that giving a unit a mechanism to explicitly model dynamic, non-linear dependencies between channels using global information can ease the learning process; they offer this as a claim motivating the design, set against prior work that assumed instance-agnostic functions with local receptive fields.
quotes: we claim that providing the unit with a mechanism to explicitly model dynamic, non-linear dependencies between channels using global information can ease the learning process
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim in Related Work; the experiments are the evidence.

assertions.value: The authors report training on ImageNet 2012 with synchronous SGD with momentum 0.9 and minibatch 1024, initial learning rate 0.6 decreased by a factor of 10 every 30 epochs, for 100 epochs from scratch, with baseline and SE models trained with identical optimisation schemes and reduction ratio 16 by default.
quotes: momentum 0.9 and a minibatch size of 1024
The initial learning rate is set to 0.6 and decreased by a factor of 10 every 30 epochs.
Models are trained for 100 epochs from scratch
Each baseline network architecture and its corresponding SE counterpart are trained with identical optimisation schemes.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own training setup in Section 5.1.
assertions.reader_inference: The value 16 for r is stated on p.5 ('set to 16 by default') and is not in the quotes given here.

assertions.value: The authors state that, for a fair comparison, they re-train the baseline models and report the scores in a re-implementation column, alongside the results reported in the original papers.
quotes: we re-train the baseline models and report the scores in the re-implementation column
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated evaluation protocol in the caption.
assertions.reader_inference: No repeated runs or variance estimates are reported for the single-crop errors.

assertions.value: The authors report that their best SENet ensemble achieves 2.251% top-5 error on the ILSVRC 2017 test set, roughly a 25% relative improvement over the previous year's winner (2.991%).
quotes: Our best model ensemble achieves a 2.251% top-5 error on the test
This represents roughly a 25% relative improvement when compared to the winner entry of the previous year (top-5 error of 2.991%).
assertions.certainty_reason: A competition result reported by the authors; the test set is evaluated by the organisers.

assertions.value: The authors state that the winning entry was a small ensemble of SENets using a standard multi-scale and multi-crop fusion strategy to obtain 2.251% top-5 test error.
quotes: Our winning entry comprised a small ensemble of SENets that employed a standard multi-scale and multi-crop fusion strategy
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors describe the composition of their own submission.

assertions.value: The authors report that ResNet-50 needs about 3.86 GFLOPs per forward pass at 224 × 224 input, and SE-ResNet-50 with reduction ratio 16 about 3.87 GFLOPs, a 0.26% relative increase.
quotes: ResNet-50 requires ∼3.86 GFLOPs in a single forward pass for a 224 × 224 pixel input image.
r (introduced in Section 3.2) to 16, SE-ResNet-50 requires ∼3.87 GFLOPs, corresponding to a 0.26% relative increase over the original ResNet-50.
assertions.certainty_reason: Measured computational cost for one architecture pair.

assertions.value: The authors report a forward-and-backward pass through ResNet-50 taking 190 ms versus 209 ms for SE-ResNet-50 with a training minibatch of 256 images, on a server with 8 NVIDIA Titan X GPUs.
quotes: a single pass forwards and backwards through ResNet-50 takes 190 ms, compared to 209 ms for SE-ResNet-50 with a training minibatch of 256 images
both timings are performed on a server with 8 NVIDIA Titan X GPUs
assertions.certainty_reason: Timing measured on one setup.
assertions.reader_inference: Roughly a 10% runtime overhead on GPU versus a 0.26% FLOP increase.

assertions.value: The authors report CPU inference time for a 224 × 224 input of 164 ms for ResNet-50 versus 167 ms for SE-ResNet-50.
quotes: ResNet-50 takes 164 ms in comparison to 167 ms for SE-ResNet-50
assertions.certainty_reason: Single timing measurement.

assertions.value: The authors report that SE-ResNet-50 introduces about 2.5 million additional parameters beyond the roughly 25 million of ResNet-50, about a 10% increase, mostly from the final stage.
quotes: SE-ResNet-50 introduces ∼2.5 million additional parameters beyond the
∼25 million parameters required by ResNet-50, corresponding to a ∼10% increase.
assertions.certainty_reason: Reported parameter count for one architecture.

assertions.value: The authors report that removing the SE blocks of the final stage costs under 0.1% top-5 error on ImageNet and reduces the relative parameter increase to about 4%.
quotes: (<0.1% top-5 error on ImageNet) reducing the relative parameter increase to ∼4%
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical statement; no table is given for this variant in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is stated in prose only, without a table.

assertions.value: The authors report that SE-ResNet-50 reaches 6.62% single-crop top-5 validation error versus 7.48% for ResNet-50, and that SE-ResNet-101 (6.07%) outperforms the deeper ResNet-152 (6.34%).
quotes: SE-ResNet-50 achieves a single-crop top-5 validation error of 6.62%, exceeding ResNet-50 (7.48%) by 0.86%
SE-ResNet-101 (6.07% top-5 error) not only matches, but outperforms the deeper ResNet-152 network (6.34% top-5 error) by 0.27%
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result reported without repeated runs.

assertions.value: The authors report that SE-ResNet-50 approaches ResNet-101 (6.52% top-5 error) with about half the computational burden (3.87 GFLOPs versus 7.58 GFLOPs).
quotes: ResNet-101 network (6.52% top-5 error)
3.87 GFLOPs vs. 7.58 GFLOPs
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical comparison.

assertions.value: The authors report that SE-ResNeXt-50 reaches 5.49% top-5 error, better than ResNeXt-50 (5.90%) and the deeper ResNeXt-101 (5.57%).
quotes: SE-ResNeXt-50 has a top-5 error of 5.49% which is superior to both its direct counterpart ResNeXt-50 (5.90%
top-5 error) as well as the deeper ResNeXt-101 (5.57% top-5 error)
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical single comparison.

assertions.value: The authors report that SE-Inception-ResNet-v2 (4.79% top-5 error) outperforms their re-implemented Inception-ResNet-v2 baseline (5.21%) by 0.42%.
quotes: SE counterpart (4.79% top-5 error) outperforms our reimplemented Inception-ResNet-v2 baseline (5.21% top-5 error) by 0.42%
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical single comparison.

assertions.value: The authors report that SE blocks improve performance on the non-residual VGG-16 (with batch normalization added) and BN-Inception architectures.
quotes: we observe that SE blocks bring improvements in performance on the non-residual settings.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result.
assertions.reader_inference: Table 2 gives VGG-16 top-5 8.81 to 7.70 and BN-Inception 7.89 to 7.14.

assertions.value: The authors report that SE blocks consistently improve the accuracy of MobileNet and ShuffleNet by a large margin at a minimal increase in computational cost.

the accuracy by a large margin at a minimal increase in computational cost.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result.
assertions.reader_inference: Table 3: MobileNet top-1 28.4 to 25.3, ShuffleNet 32.6 to 31.0; params 4.2M to 4.7M and 1.8M to 2.4M.

assertions.value: The authors report that SENet versions had lower CIFAR-10 error than the baselines in every comparison, with original errors 6.37, 5.46, 4.27, 2.56 versus SENet 5.21, 4.39, 3.88, 2.12 (percent).
quotes: We observe that in every comparison SENets outperform the baseline architectures
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result, single runs.
assertions.reader_inference: Baselines in order: ResNet-110, ResNet-164, WRN-16-8, Shake-Shake+Cutout.

assertions.value: The authors report CIFAR-100 errors of 26.88, 24.33, 20.43, 15.85 (percent) for the baselines versus 23.85, 21.31, 19.14, 15.41 for the SENet counterparts.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result, single runs.
assertions.reader_inference: Baselines in order: ResNet-110, ResNet-164, WRN-16-8, Shake-Even+Cutout.

assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result.

assertions.value: The authors report that, as the Faster R-CNN trunk, SE-ResNet-50 outperforms ResNet-50 by 2.4 points of AP (a relative 6.3% improvement) and 3.1 points on AP@IoU=0.5, and SE-ResNet-101 improves AP by 2.0 points (5.0% relative).
quotes: SE-ResNet-50 outperforms ResNet-50 by 2.4% (a relative 6.3% improvement)
and by 3.1% on AP@IoU=0.5
a 2.0% improvement (5.0% relative improvement) on the AP metric

assertions.value: The authors report that SENet-154 achieves 18.68% top-1 and 4.47% top-5 error with a 224 × 224 centre crop, which they describe as the strongest reported result in that comparison.

using a 224 × 224 centre crop evaluation, which represents the strongest reported result

assertions.value: The authors note that later results are stronger and attribute the best overall performance to a ResNeXt-101 32×48d model pretrained on about one billion weakly labelled images, which they say may be complementary to their architecture changes.
quotes: The best overall performance was reported by [80] using a ResNeXt-101 32×48d architecture.
pretraining their model on approximately one billion weakly labelled images
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

quotes: Training was performed with 8 servers (64 GPUs) in parallel to enable large batch sizes (2048).
The initial learning rate was set to 1.0.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated training setup in the appendix.

assertions.value: The authors state that all ablation experiments were run on ImageNet on a single machine with 8 GPUs, using ResNet-50 as backbone, with the learning rate starting at 0.1 and training until validation loss plateaus (about 300 epochs in total); they also removed the FC biases in the excitation operation.
quotes: All ablation experiments are performed on the ImageNet dataset on a single machine (with 8 GPUs). ResNet-50 is used as the backbone architecture.
the learning rate is initialised to 0.1 and training continues until the validation loss plateaus
removing the biases of the FC layers in the excitation operation facilitates the modelling of channel dependencies
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the scope and protocol of its ablations.
assertions.reader_inference: The 300 epochs figure appears in the same sentence group as '(∼300 epochs in total)'.

assertions.value: The authors report SE-ResNet-50 top-5 errors of 6.00, 6.09, 5.99, 6.03 and 6.20 (percent) for reduction ratios 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32, versus 6.55 for the original ResNet-50, with parameters falling from 45.7M to 26.9M.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical ablation, single runs.

assertions.value: The authors state that performance is robust to a range of reduction ratios, that increased complexity does not improve performance monotonically, and that r = 16 achieves a good balance between accuracy and complexity.
quotes: The comparison in Table 10 shows that performance is robust to a range of reduction ratios.
Setting r = 16 achieves a good balance between accuracy and complexity.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical conclusion from one ablation.

assertions.value: The authors state that using an identical reduction ratio throughout a network may not be optimal because layers play different roles, so tuning ratios per layer might improve results.
quotes: using an identical ratio throughout a network may not be optimal
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the limit of their uniform-ratio setting.

assertions.value: The authors report that both max and average pooling are effective as the squeeze operator, with average pooling slightly better, and that SE performance is fairly robust to the choice of aggregation operator.
quotes: While both max and average pooling are effective, average pooling achieves slightly better performance
the performance of SE blocks is fairly robust to the choice of speciﬁc aggregation operator
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical ablation.

assertions.value: The authors report that replacing the sigmoid with tanh slightly worsens performance, while ReLU is dramatically worse and drops SE-ResNet-50 below the ResNet-50 baseline, with top-5 errors of 6.98, 6.38 and 6.03 (percent) for ReLU, tanh and sigmoid.
quotes: exchanging the sigmoid for tanh slightly worsens performance
using ReLU is dramatically worse and in fact causes the performance of SE-ResNet-50 to drop below that of the ResNet-50 baseline
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical ablation.

assertions.value: The authors report that SE blocks added to ResNet-50 one stage at a time each help, with top-5 errors of 6.55 for the baseline, 6.48, 6.32 and 6.22 for stages 2, 3 and 4, and 6.03 with SE at all stages, and say the gains are complementary.
quotes: the gains induced by SE blocks at different stages are complementary

assertions.value: The authors report that SE-PRE, SE-Identity and the standard SE block perform similarly well while SE-POST leads to a drop in performance, with top-5 errors of 6.03, 6.00, 6.35 and 6.15 (percent) for SE, SE-PRE, SE-POST and SE-Identity.
quotes: We observe that the SE-PRE, SE-Identity and proposed SE block each perform similarly well, while usage

assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical ablation.

assertions.value: The authors suggest that improvements from SE units are fairly robust to their location, provided they are applied prior to branch aggregation.
quotes: provided that they are applied prior to branch aggregation
assertions.certainty_reason: An authors' interpretation drawn from the integration ablation.

assertions.value: The authors report that placing the SE block after the 3 × 3 convolution inside the residual unit gives comparable accuracy with fewer parameters than the standard SE block.
quotes: accuracy with fewer parameters than the standard SE block
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical ablation.

assertions.value: The authors state that a rigorous theoretical analysis of learned representations remains challenging, so they take an empirical approach to understanding the SE block, aiming only at a primitive understanding of its practical function.
quotes: A rigorous theoretical analysis of the representations learned by deep neural networks remains challenging
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the scope of their analysis.

assertions.value: The authors report that removing the global pooling (NoSqueeze) gives top-5 error 6.39% versus 6.03% for SE and 6.55% for ResNet-50, with 4.27 versus 3.87 GFLOPs, and conclude that global information matters.

assertions.value: The authors report that the distribution of excitation activations across different classes is very similar at earlier layers of the network, which they take to suggest that channel importance is shared across classes in early stages.
quotes: the distribution across different classes is very similar at the earlier layers of the network
assertions.certainty_reason: Qualitative reading of plots from four sampled classes.

assertions.value: The authors report that at greater depth the value of each channel becomes much more class-specific, as different classes show different preferences to the discriminative value of features, consistent with earlier work on feature specificity.
quotes: depth, the value of each channel becomes much more

an SE block reduces to the identity operator
are less important than previous blocks in providing recalibration to the network
